steps.text: Stir crushed vanilla wafers, 3/4 cup confectioners' sugar, cocoa, and nuts together in a large bowl. Blend in corn syrup and rum.
Shape into 1 inch balls, and roll in additional confectioners' sugar.
Store in an airtight container for several days to develop the flavor. Roll again in confectioners' sugar before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Rum Balls
raw_recipe.description: Whip up a batch of these chocolate rum balls with crushed vanilla wafers, cocoa, rum, and copped walnuts for a favorite festive treat!
raw_recipe.name: Chocolate Rum Balls

review.reviewBody: These are AWESOME!!! My husband suggested an easier way to coat them with the powdered sugar: instead of rolling them in it, put the sugar in a ziploc bag and shake. They come out perfect with less mess to clean up!

Need 10 stars for this recipe!! So quick, easy, and awesome! My dough seemed a little dry, so I added about 2T evaporated milk , and it worked great. I covered with plastic and refrigerated it overnight before rolling into balls. For coating, I used 2 gallon size ziploc bags. One filled with powdered sugar, dropped the balls in as I rolled them. When getting full, I shook the bag, then moved those into the empty bag for storage. Refrigerated for 2 days, then threw in more powdered sugar and shook it again before serving. This made them resemble fluffy little snowballs. Everyone loved these, and they're already begging me to make more. Thanks!!

Rumballs are what is always requested of me so I like to make sure I'm using good recipe. This is it. BUT, I omit adding icing sugar to the mix. Sweet enough for us once they are double-rolled in it. What i do do that I think bumps it up a notch or two is pouring some rum and Irish cream in a bowl and roll the balls around in it, place them on a cookie sheet to freeze and then bag and return to the freezer until I am ready to pull them out. Then I thaw and toss in the icing sugar. Adds extra little boozy kick (insert wink emoji here)

I hate to review something I altered but.. here goes. I used my food processor to grind the Nilla Wafers ( 2 cups), I used pecans and ground those also ( 2 cups), added 2 cups confectioner's sugar and 4 teaspoons unsweetened cocoa powder... then added 1 t. Vietnamese cinnamon, 1/2 t. Nutmeg and 1/4 t. ground cloves.. stir well in large bowl with a whisk. In measuring cup I poured 1/2 c. SPICED RUM and 4 t. Light Karo.. stir until well blended and then pour over cookie mix. stir till all is dampened and let it sit for about 10 minutes to soak it up. form into 1" balls, roll in conf. sugar and store in refrigerator. these are the bomb! and super easy.. no baking!

I used this recipe for proportions. I didn't have vanilla wafers, but I did have Nabisco chocolate wafers bought for an unmade cheesecake crust. 

Very potent right out of the bowl but by morning and a second roll in powdered sugar, they were just what my dad wanted.

I also made a second batch and divided the dry ingredients. I made one half with Chambord, melting a teaspoon of raspberry jam that I mixed with the corn syrup (reducing it by 1 tsp). Into the remaining half of the dry ingredients, I stirred 1/2 teaspoon of orange zest and used Grand Marnier. Both are a nice variation on this recipe.

Delicious and extremely versatile recipe. I've used both vanilla wafers and if I didn't have any on hand, I've also used shortbread cookies. Try mixing some up with either coconut rum or spiced rum and add some coconut for added texture. I've used almonds, pecans and walnuts. Also used this recipe with high quality bourbon or whiskey for a smoother taste. I use a 1 1/4" cookie scoop for mess free and evenly sized balls. Roll them into balls and freeze on a tray. Once frozen, I put them into a container and put back into the freezer allow to meld for a few days. When ready to serve, remove from freezer, immediately roll or shake into ziplock of powdered sugar but you only need a thin coating, then allow to thaw some before rolling into more powdered sugar or nuts, toasted coconut, sugar, etc. Always a hit and so easy to make with ingredients I have on hand.

Perfect ratios for this classic recipe. Use a food processor to really get your Nilla wafers down to powder and make them 1-2 weeks ahead, not just a few days. It really helps the texture and flavor. Also, I don't see a yield on the recipe, but I use a cookie scoop to portion the dough into 2-teaspoon balls, and get a little over 3 dozen. People will be happy to eat these right out of the container, but if you want them to look perfect on a tray, plan to re-coat them before serving, otherwise they get a bit squished in storage and some of the rum soaks through the sugar. I roll in a mix of cocoa and powdered sugar.

Rum balls are strong, people. They're supposed to be very rummy. They are NOT supposed to be a sweet sugary cookie. If you don't like rum or nuts, don't make them. I don't know why people make things with major ingredients they don't like and then complain that they don't like the finished product. I think these are great and I've made them with other types of liquor and nuts. For those who don't know, you're supposed to use Nilla Wafers (or whatever brand you can find) and crush them really fine, like in a food processor. You can use a blender to crush them, but don't dump the whole box in - do a handful at a time. This takes longer, but you need to give the blender blades room to work.

I've made several batches of these every Christmas for about 13 years because my friends and relatives won't let me stop! They are a tradition and favorite. A few things I've learned through the years: I use my food processor for the wafers and the walnuts creating almost a powder. This helps them roll better and the flavor is smoother. The best rum to use is Black Strap Rum as it has dark molasses undertones. Finally I add a little more corn syrup to create the right consistency for rolling the balls with no messy hands. I roll them and place on wax paper then when done, add groups to a bag of confectioners sugar (much easier and less messy than rolling in the sugar). I place them in an air tight container for several days and sometimes a couple of weeks. The flavor gets better and smoother. My mother used to make her fruit cake three weeks before Christmas and know I understand why.

These are amazing! If I don't make these every Christmas the (adult) kids will complain! I crush the vanilla wafers and chop the walnuts in the food processor, sometimes I sub honey for the corn syrup. I usually use Captain Morgan's spiced rum but this year I'm going to try black strap rum. I usually have to dust these in the powdered sugar for a second coating prior to packing in Christmas boxes. Be sure and let these sit for several days or the rum will be too sharp. They need time to mellow. Christmas tradition!

these are amaaaaazing! 3 boxes of wafers makes 100- I use special dark coco, toast the walnuts or hubby ‘s fav is when I use pecans toasted! after you mix let mixture set covered for 3-4 hours/ it is way easier to roll / don’t t stick to your hands ad much. I use a cookie scoop. I sprinkle them with chocolate pixie/ disco dust- edible glitter- do beautiful
Easy to make, great tasting. No changes.
I made mine with bourbon & pecans. With the chocolate, Oh My! Will definitely be added to the recipe collection

I made exact recipe. I wasn't sure how much to crush the nilla wafers. I pulsed them in a food processor to a "grapenut" look. I found then hard to keep together when rolling. Anyway, I found I needed more than one batch for a party so, back to the store for more wafers. This time I went for more of a flour consistency, like corn meal. I also ran out of rum so I went with Kalhua. I found these ones much easier to roll out.
These were great! I added more rum and soaked the nuts in the rum and karo syrup before adding to the rest of the ingredients.
Loved this recipe, easy and simple

Easy recipe, they always turn out great. Making these always takes me back to my younger days when my mom used to make them during the Christmas holiday. It’s a tradition that I’ll never forget and now I get requests for them. I’m carrying on the tradition, and I love it.
This was not very tasty, not sweet enough, I made it before with coffee and more powered sugar. For those who like less sweetness it would be ok.
My mom made these, but with bourbon, in the 1950s to send to my Naval Officer dad when he had to be away on a ship at Christmas. I’ve been making them all my adult life and they are still a hit.
This is a great base recipe! It allows you to make small changes so you can personalize it. I add drunk cherries.
